title: Localized numeric abbreviation and accessible tooltip behavior for metric cards
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Problem: Metric cards in the Cost Explorer and Dashboards currently abbreviate large numbers using a simple ASCII suffix (e.g., 1.2K, 3.4M). This creates multiple issues for internationalization and accessibility: (1) some locales use non-ASCII grouping and different magnitude words (e.g., 1,2k vs 1.2K vs 1,2 Tsd), (2) screen readers often read 'K' as 'kay' which is confusing, (3) truncation removes contextual units (tokens / requests / $) and tooltip behavior is inconsistent and not reliably keyboard/focus accessible. Goal: define a localized numeric-abbreviation strategy and an accessible tooltip interaction pattern for metric cards that works across locales (including RTL), across assistive tech, and on keyboard-only / touch devices.
proposal_summary: 1) Replace hard-coded ASCII suffixes with an i18n-aware display layer that chooses localized short forms where available and falls back to full localized numbers for screen readers. 2) Add an explicit, persistent accessible label for each metric card (visually hidden) that contains the full localized number + unit so SR users get context. 3) Standardize tooltip triggers so the same content is reachable by hover, keyboard focus (Tab -> Enter/Space toggles), and long-press on touch. 4) For RTL locales ensure abbreviations and unit order follow locale conventions. 5) Provide a console toggle in Settings to disable abbreviation for precision workflows.
design_decisions:
- Use ICU message patterns for short number formatting where supported by CLDR; fallback to localized full numbers for screen-reader text.
- Tooltip content will be the canonical localized string: e.g., '$1,240.00 per 1k tokens' or localized equivalent.
- Implement a visually-hidden element with aria-live='polite' that announces metric changes; on focus enter/space will announce the full value via aria-describedby to link tooltip to card.
- Keyboard: Tab focuses card, Enter/Space opens tooltip; Esc closes. Tooltip will trap focus when open and include a close button.
- For compact views where truncation would hide unit, the card must always render the unit in the accessible label even if visually truncated.
- Analytics: add event `metric_card_tooltip_open` with properties locale, metric_key, abbreviation_used, opened_by (keyboard/mouse/touch).
acceptance_criteria: Short-form numbers use locale-aware abbreviations when available (CLDR) otherwise show localized full number in SR text.
Screen reader announces full value + unit when card receives focus or when tooltip opens (tested in VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS).
Tooltip reachable and operable by mouse hover, keyboard (Tab -> Enter/Space), and touch long-press; focus is trapped while tooltip open and Esc/close button restore focus to card.
RTL locales render abbreviation/unit order according to locale rules and maintain correct aria relationships.
Settings toggle disables abbreviation and persists per user; QA verifies persisted preference across sessions.
Telemetry events emitted for tooltip opens with correct metadata.
Unit tests for formatting library fallbacks and storybook examples for at least en-US, fr-FR, pt-BR, ja-JP, ar-SA.
Design review sign-off from Accessibility and Internationalization leads and one PM will approve rollout gating.
Performance: no more than 6ms median added render latency for metric card initial paint across typical dashboard payloads.
implementation_notes: Eng should integrate ICU-short-number patterns where available; where platform lacks CLDR short patterns ship a small mapping table maintained in i18n repo. Keep presentation and sr-only text derived from same localization key to avoid divergence. Discuss with infra/analytics prior to telemetry implementation. Add E2E scenarios in Playwright to assert keyboard interactions and SR announcements using axe-core hooks.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Rao: Initial write-up and prototype uploaded. Asked ENG for feasibility of ICU short number support in the web runtime. Assigned to Miguel to run a quick audit.

2026-03-04 - Miguel Torres: Audit complete — browser Intl.NumberFormat supports compact notation for most locales except some legacy browsers. Proposed fallback mapping for critical locales (ar-SA, ja-JP). Raised ENG-66212 to track runtime integration.

2026-03-05 - Accessibility Review (Leah Park): Reviewed prototype. Ask: prefer aria-describedby linking to the tooltip element rather than relying only on aria-live for persistent clarity. Also recommend using role='dialog' for tooltip when it traps focus.
2026-03-06 - PM (Diego Mendes): Confirmed metric unit phrasing must come from product vocabulary (tokens vs token-requests). Added PM-1447 to define canonical unit strings per metric.

2026-03-08 - Miguel Torres: Updated Figma with keyboard interaction states and added a11y binding notes. Implemented Storybook stories for en/fr/pt/ja/ar and basic axe checks. PR open: github.com/redwood/console/pull/12345

2026-03-09 - Aisha Rao: Design review notes applied — adjusted tooltip layout to avoid overlapping density controls, improved focus ring for high-contrast mode. Requesting final sign-off from i18n lead and accessibility lead.
2026-03-10 - Leah Park: Sign-off provided pending implementation tests for VoiceOver with compact notation; marked as In Review.
qa_checklist: Validate localized short/long number rendering across target locales.
Keyboard-only walkthrough: Tab -> Enter opens tooltip, Tab cycles within tooltip, Esc closes and focus returns to card.
Screen readers: VoiceOver/NVDA/JAWS read full localized metric and unit on focus and on tooltip open.
RTL verification: ordering, punctuation, and tooltip placement do not break layout.
Settings toggle persistence verified across browsers and devices.
Telemetry events observed with expected schema and locale metadata.
notes: This ticket focuses on presentation and interaction — numeric aggregation/rounding policy (how we compute costs) is out of scope and will be handled in a separate PM ticket. Be wary of regressions in low-bandwidth dashboards — lazy-formatting preferred.
